defects: Seed 1, B-WHOLE and B-BARE: numerous long, straight, similarly sized ascending branches produce a crowded broom-like framework and upright foliage streaks. This overwhelms the spreading, progressively subdivided branch structure visible in the beech references.

Seed 1, B-BARE: multiple substantial branches terminate abruptly in blunt ends, particularly around the upper crown. Their repeated appearance reads as a construction artifact rather than the fine terminal branching shown in reference-1.
observations: Passes follow the required-cell order: B-WHOLE reference_character, then B-BARE reference_character.
Acceptable variation: the references support differences in crown breadth, asymmetry and foliage density; an identical silhouette is unnecessary.
Optional refinement: the conspicuous horizontal bark markings could be softened toward the smoother gray surface in reference-1. Photographic lichen detail is unnecessary.
The left crown is clipped in both renders, so complete crown width and balance remain unknown.
The accepted spruce anchor supports a simplified catalogue rendering style; its species morphology is not a beech requirement.
No earlier candidate is supplied, so relative improvement cannot be established.

findings.observation: B-WHOLE reference_character fails: seed 1 has a broadly rounded leafy crown, but its interior is dominated by repeated upright foliage columns and conspicuous straight ascending limbs. Reference-0 instead shows more spreading, laterally articulated foliage masses. B-BARE confirms that the dominant directional pattern belongs to the shared framework.

B-BARE reference_character fails: seed 1 exposes a dense array of long, relatively uniform straight limbs, with repeated blunt substantial tips around the upper crown. Reference-1 shows a more differentiated hierarchy resolving into fine branching. The repeated abrupt endings are visible construction artifacts even at a stylized finish floor.
The broad deciduous crown, exposed lower trunk and branching scaffold provide a grounded partial match to the supplied beech photographs. These matches do not resolve the dominant framework defects.

The bare render reveals the same seed's geometry with foliage hidden. It therefore constrains interpretation of the leafy render; it does not demonstrate a seasonal or load-induced change. The photographs have no documented specimen relationship.
